claim: A 'failed' Reproducibility Project: Psychology replication of a fertility/mate-preference effect is restored to statistical significance after controlling for a stimulus-allocation confound absent from the original study.
stance_target: N9 - precedent for audit strengthening a finding
scope_conditions: psychology, Open Science Collaboration Reproducibility Project: Psychology, US replication sample
quoted_support: I show that the "failed replication" datasets contain a gross bias in stimulus allocation which is absent in the original dataset; controlling for it replicates the original study's main finding.

claim: Under a stricter (tighter) alternative specification of the fertile-window definition, the reanalyzed effect became stronger, not weaker.
stance_target: N9 - precedent for audit strengthening a finding
quoted_support: the results came out stronger using the stricter window (days 10-15) defined as "peak fertility" in Gildersleeve et al.'s (2014) meta-analysis.
